<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via validateWidgetBindings (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via validateWidgetBindings (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `127e4876fd63c3f2e0b1b3c19ea14acc47687caa` — the merge of head `29690d3da63d99cdb5b0647dab163a13d473d625` into base `0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 127e4876fd63c3f2e0b1b3c19ea14acc47687caa && git checkout 127e4876fd63c3f2e0b1b3c19ea14acc47687caa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76 29690d3da63d99cdb5b0647dab163a13d473d625 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76 && git merge --no-ff 29690d3da63d99cdb5b0647dab163a13d473d625

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `29690d3da63d99cdb5b0647dab163a13d473d625`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/lint/src/validate-report-runtime-filter.ts` + test, `validate-widget-bindings.ts` (full diff vs `origin/main`, plus the head's call site and `const graph`), `reference-integrity-suite.ts` + test, `index.ts`, `rule-explanations.ts`, `runtime-gate.inert-type-writes.test.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.dashboard-dataset-publish-gate.test.ts`, `.changeset/29900-report-runtime-filter-field-unknown.md`, `packages/lint/package.json` (`exports`). Cited code read, not reviewed: `filter-walk.ts`, `object-graph.ts`, `runtime-gate.ts` (`buildRuntimeWriteSnapshots`), `service-analytics` (`declaredMemberEntry`, `resolveMemberSource`, `assertWhereFields`, `dataset-filter-field-binding.ts`), `ui/packages/plugin-report/src/DatasetReportRenderer.tsx`, `spec/src/ui/report.zod.ts`. Rules: `contract-review.md`, `review-checklist.md`, `SKILL.md:313`, AGENTS.md step 3, `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, `record-recognisers.mjs`. Precedents: `fa1eca3` (the twin), `ae7f49e` (#26928). Card #29900 + 6601984965, 6618416942, 6620560871; the order; the dev report JSON; head and merge-base check-runs; #29991, #29992.

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on PR body and changeset), no published schema. Run in-seat as an isolated reviewer at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, fed the card, the PR and the head's check-runs only.

### ① Derived judgments
- **Accept set of `report-filter-field-unknown`: correct, a strict subset of the twin's refusals.** The judgement is the twin's `judgeDatasetFilterKeys`; the report arm then drops any bare key naming a `dimensions[].name` of the bound dataset. Accepted: object fields (hop by hop), registry-injected system columns (`created_at` pinned), dotted relationship paths, `$and`/`$or`/`$not` walked and other `$` keys skipped, the `{field, operator}` and `[field, op, value]` shapes, and bare dimension names. Skipped: a dataset resolving to nothing (`chart-dataset-unknown` owns it), an object absent from the stack or snapshot.
- **Dimension acceptance is right; the twin is the one that is wrong.** `dataset-filter-field-binding.ts` and `assertWhereFields` → `resolveMemberSource(cube, member, 'any')` bind a bare dimension name at run time. The rules disagree only in the direction the ruling asked (report ⊂ twin), so this is a twin false positive on main today, not a report defect (③).
- **Residual false positive, shared with the twin and within the ruling's bound: a bare dataset MEASURE name.** `declaredMemberEntry(…, 'any')` falls through to `cube.measures`, so `runtimeFilter: { hours_sum: { $gt: 3 } }` renders, yet both rules refuse it. This is not a breach of "do not refuse more than the twin", and the order listed dimensions only, so it is carried, not reworked (③).
- **No false negative beyond the cross-package one.** On a `joined` report, the container filter is judged against each block's dataset and the block filter against its own, which matches the renderer's `mergeFilters(outerFilter, block.runtimeFilter)`. Every report `type` binds `dataset`.
- **Doors.** Suite member with `runtimeTypes: ['flow','report']`, after `validateReportDateRange`, so `os validate`, `os build`, `os lint` and the report publish door all run it. Pinned at the door's snapshot shape and through the real `saveMetaItem` → `publishMetaItem` (draft→publish 422 at `reports[0].runtimeFilter.no_such_field`, active save 422, field, dimension and `$and` + system column publish, dashboard control unchanged). `defineStack` runs no lint rule, and the twin does not reach it either.
- **The extraction preserves behaviour for `widget-filter-field-unknown` and `widget-filter-field-not-included`: no verdict changes.** Compared line by line, the guards, skips, `joinablePrefixes`, walker path, `resolveFieldPath` / `isUnjudgeable` / `describeFieldPathVerdict`, and the not-included test are all the same. Rule ids, severity, paths, messages and hints are unchanged, `indexResolvableDatasets` is the old map code moved verbatim, and `validate-widget-bindings.test.ts` is untouched.
- **Public surface.** The entry gains `validateReportRuntimeFilters`, `REPORT_FILTER_FIELD_UNKNOWN` and type `ReportRuntimeFilterFinding`. The helpers are re-exported through none of `.`, `./runtime` or `./rule-explanations`. `RULE_EXPLANATIONS` gains the entry its test requires.

### ② Semver level
`@objectstack/lint` **minor**, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, a BREAKING banner and `!` in the title, consistent with AGENTS.md step 3 and with the twin (`fa1eca3`, which landed minor: "this narrows the accept set"; it predates the declaration lines). **Arm:** `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is grammatical and honest (the new entry exports widen the surface ⇒ `yes`; the arm records the BREAKING narrowing), and `record-recognisers.mjs` routes it to this face, so the claim's provisional `no (narrowing)` was correctly revised. **ADR-0087:** `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is in `CATEGORIES`, in the same shape as `ae7f49e`; there is correctly no FROM → TO, because nothing authorable is removed or renamed. **Skills-docs:** the line is present and its substance is true, but its value `no move — …` is outside the closed vocabulary at `SKILL.md:313` (`updated here | follow-up owed — FILES | follow-up #N | none — REASON`). It must read `none — …` in both the PR body and the changeset, which ships verbatim into the CHANGELOG. **Check-runs at review:** 25 success, 9 skipped, 26 in progress, 0 failures.

### ③ Boundary flags
- **Cross-package gap, confirmed; the seat files it.** `buildRuntimeWriteSnapshots` reduces `objects` (and only `objects`) to the written item's package closure. `datasets` is not narrowed, so a dataset outside the closure resolves while its object is absent, and skip 1 silences both filter-key rules.
- **Twin vs cube member vocabulary; the seat files one card carrying both halves.** (a) The twin refuses a bare dimension name the dataset door binds. (b) Both rules refuse a bare measure name the dataset door binds. The correct bare-key accept set is fields ∪ injected columns ∪ dimensions ∪ measures.
- **Dogfood "pre-existing" claim: credible.** The merge-base `9049be26` has `Dogfood Regression Gate (2/3)` failing (run 41739314629). #29991 filed it as main-red, and #29992 (`0b99c2b1`, now on `main`) fixes exactly those two cases. A merge of `main` clears it.
- A container key on a `joined` report yields one finding per block at the same container path. Informational.
- Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; `open_questions`: none.

### ④ Narrowing face
- `validate-report-runtime-filter.ts` stands against the acceptance scenario, and its joined handling matches the renderer's merge. `validate-widget-bindings.ts` is a refactor only. The suite order pin and the "report reaches THREE members" pin are updated.
- Pins adequate: 12 unit cases including the parity pin, door-shape LIT/CONTROL, the real route, the dashboard control, `validate`/`build` command pins, one ablation (10/52 lint + 2/4 metadata-protocol red, controls green, restore verified), and a shipped-corpus sweep with 0 findings plus a positive control.
- Changeset: declarations, banner and disposition correct; the `Skills-docs:` token is off-grammar (②).
